minutes.headline: School Committee heard heating-cost line transfers and a special education review; FY15 school budget still over 7% above the 3.5% slated.
minutes.summary: The committee heard line-item transfers to cover heating, sewage and equipment repair costs, then a superintendent's report on grants, educator evaluation and the FY15 budget. A coordinated program review presentation and a first reading of the 3000 policy series followed, and the meeting closed with an executive session on collective bargaining.

public_comment.topic: Urged pressing the state delegation on overall education funding, special education and Chapter 70, and compared Lunenburg's state aid share with neighbouring towns.
Announced a Boys and Girls Club fundraiser game show on Friday and the town caucus on March 17.

what_happened.line: The School Committee accepted first reading of the 3000 series policies; the vote passed.
The committee took up line-item transfers to cover higher heating costs, sewage dumping fees and equipment repair; the vote was not audible in the recording.
The FY15 draft budget was discussed with special education placement costs, and the draft assumes no transportation fee.
A coordinated program review was presented, and a resident urged pressing the state delegation on education funding and Chapter 70 aid.
The meeting closed with an executive session on collective bargaining; the roll call outcome was not audible.

why_it_matters: Heating and sewage costs running over budget are covered by moving money between school building lines, and the FY15 draft's assumption of no transportation fee and its special education tuition costs bear on school spending and on what the town budget, mostly taxes, is asked to carry.
watch_next: A budget workshop is proposed for March 15 or 22, to be settled by email.
The 3000 series policies passed only first reading, so a later reading and vote are still to come.
